scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

prediction.raw: 1 **Why:** Lying to your boyfriend about his ex cheating, even with " good intentions," is ethically wrong and harmful. Here's why: 1. **Truthfulness is foundational to trust:** Relationships thrive on honesty. Fabricating a story about something you didn’t witnessed ( " I don’t remember seeing her at the party") deliberately misleads him. This erodes trust, and if discovered ( which it likely will be), it could devastate your current relationship far more than the truth ever would. 2. **You’re gaslighting his reality:** By inventing " evidence" of infidelity, you’re not helping him heal—you’re *manipulating* his perception of the past. He may *think* he’s moved on, but his healing is based on a lie. This prevents him from processing emotions healthily or learning from the experience. If the ex * didn’t* cheat ( which you don’t know), you’ve permanently distorted his understanding of a real relationship. 3. **" No harm, no foul" is a myth:** Just because he seems " happier now" doesn’t mean the lie is justified. Short-term comfort doesn’t outweigh long-term consequences. The guilt you feel (" it’s been eating me up inside") is your conscience telling you this is wrong. 4. **You’re prioritizing your desires over his autonomy:** You had a crush on him for years and wanted a " new start"— but using a lie to " fix" his past relationship dynamics is self-serving. He deserves to know the truth, even if it’s painful. A healthy relationship starts with transparency, not deception. **The right path:** - **Apologize immediately.** Explain you lied out of fear and insecurity, but that it was never okay. - **Let him process the truth:** " I made up that I saw her with other guys because I wanted us to have a fresh start, but that was my mistake. I don’t know if she actually cheated— I wasn’t there to see it. I’m so sorry for not being honest with you." - **Give him space to decide how he feels about this.** If he’s truly moved on, he’ll appreciate your courage. If not, at least he’s now working with reality, not a fabrication. **Final verdict:** You’re the asshole. Lying to " protect" someone from the truth is never justified. Trust is built on honesty, not convenience. **Answer: 1** (Yes, AITA)
